sections.content: How many people are "records clerks and assistants"?

109,660 people

were counted on the census as "records clerks and assistants" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Records clerks and assistants maintain and update electronic and/or hard copy documents, correspondence and other records, and organise their storage.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "records clerks and assistants" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 25 to 29 years. Of the whole working population 11.1% were aged 25 to 29 years. For people working as "records clerks and assistants", 12.4% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "records clerks and assistants" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "records clerks and assistants" included:

  • assemblers and routine operatives (other)
  • debt, rent and other cash collectors
  • bank and post office clerks

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "records clerks and assistants" there were more women than men (75.2% compared with 24.8%).

This means "records clerks and assistants" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "administrative occupations".

Men made up 24.8% and women made up 75.2% of "records clerks and assistants"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "records clerks and assistants" included:

  • professional/chartered company secretaries
  • book-keepers, payroll managers and wages clerks
  • finance officers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "records clerks and assistants" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of women with this occupation than men.

The percentage of men and women who are "records clerks and assistants" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "records clerks and assistants", 12.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (70% compared with 30%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (98%) than self-employed (2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
